newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Second blast in Albanian capital - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Second blast in Albanian capital - witnesses.

text.p: At least two people were injured in a powerful explosion at a bus station in the centre of the Albanian capital Tirana on Monday, witnesses said.
The blast occurred just minutes before a 9 p.m. (1900 GMT) curfew began, witnesses said, and came hours after a bomb in a crowded cafe injured at least 20 people.

At least two people were seen leaving the scene of the bus station blast, one limping and another with his face covered with blood, witnesses said. Police blocked off the street and technicians began examining the area.
The bus station is a few hundred metres (yards) from Skanderbeg Square where the cafe bombed earlier is located.

Albania's two main rival political parties, President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party and the Socialist Party, each accused extremists of the opposite political side of escalating tensions ahead of June 29 elections.
The early polls are intended to restore stability in the Balkan country, plunged into near anarchy by March riots ignited by the collapse of shady investment schemes.
